scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8129: One workstation in Campus 1 -- PC11, one of the
172.16.20.x machines -- has fallen off the network entirely. From that desk
you cannot reach anything: not the machines next to it, not the usual first
stop out, nothing at all. Every other desk around it is fine, and nothing
was moved or changed at that desk, so this is not something we did: the
network has dropped PC11 on your side. Look at why exactly that one machine
is cut off and put it back on today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC11 (172.16.20.x on VLAN 20) reaches its
  gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0% loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and
  reaches off-subnet destinations across the core (OSPF converged). The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a single-host
  isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC11 isolated from
everything -- is NOT reproducible: PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0%
loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and reaches off-subnet hosts (e.g. a
Campus 2 or other-VLAN address) across the converged core.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: PC11's connectivity is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces PC11's gateway,
intra-VLAN, and inter-subnet reachability, finds them working, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a disabled port or an isolated host -- blaming the
switch port, the VLAN 20 SVI, or PC11's config to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A thorough end-to-end investigation of PC11 (172.16.20.11/24) and its entire network path reveals no fault anywhere in the topology. PC11's interface eth0 is UP and correctly addressed. Its access port on switch2 (eth5) is operationally UP, assigned to the `br_vlan20` bridge domain, and has PC11's MAC address (8e:0f:9a:0d:d7:00) actively learned — exactly as expected for a healthy access port. The switch2 bridge correctly forwards VLAN 20 traffic through the eth0.20 sub-interface up to mswitch0's vlan20 SVI (172.16.20.254/24), which also shows no anomaly.

Ping tests from PC11 to every meaningful destination all return 0% packet loss: both same-VLAN neighbors PC9 (172.16.20.9) and PC10 (172.16.20.10), the VLAN 20 default gateway (172.16.20.254), cross-VLAN destinations on VLAN 10 (172.16.10.5) and VLAN 30 (172.16.30.12), and the simulated WAN host (55.5.1.1). The one destination that does not respond — 8.8.8.8 — is equally unreachable from PC9 and PC10, confirming it is a lab-wide baseline limitation (no real internet) and completely unrelated to PC11.

The ticket's claim that PC11 "has fallen off the network entirely" and cannot reach even its immediate neighbors is not supported by any live measurement. The premise of the trouble ticket is false: PC11 is fully connected at both L2 and L3, and no fault exists in the network.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254, same-VLAN hosts, and off-subnet destinations with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly shows 0% loss to the gateway 172.16.20.254, same-VLAN hosts (PC9/PC10), and off‑subnet destinations, confirming a healthy baseline.

The agent's conclusions are directly supported by the logged commands and outputs (interface state, FDB, ip routes, and multiple ping results showing 0% loss between PC11, its gateway, VLAN peers, and cross-VLAN/WAN hosts). The inference that the ticket describes a false positive (lab baseline for 8.8.8.8) follows logically from comparative tests across multiple hosts.
